title: Buying Time, Softening Excuses & Steering a Talk

sections.content: You know *No es que* + subjunctive, *sino que* + indicative from B2 Unit 5. In live conversation, speakers also gain a second to think or steer a talk back on track with short spoken formulas: *a ver…* ('let's see…') buys time before answering, *es que…* ('it's just that…') softens a refusal or explanation, and *ir al grano* / *sin rodeos* cut short a digression (*el inciso*) when someone starts to *salirse del tema*. Notice how spoken Spanish often pairs B2's *No es que* + subjunctive with *es que* + indicative in informal speech: *No es que no quiera ir, es que tengo demasiado trabajo*.

sections.title: Spoken hesitation, excuses and steering
rows: Buys thinking time before answering (*A ver, déjame pensar un momento.*).
Softens an excuse or refusal (*Es que hoy salgo tarde de la oficina.*).
Spoken counterpart to *no es que… sino que…* (*No es que esté cansado, es que tengo frío.*).
*ir al grano* ('get to the point'), *sin rodeos* ('straight out'), *salirse del tema* / *volver al tema*.

items.spanish: A ver, sin rodeos: ¿puedes terminar la parte del informe antes del viernes?
items.english: Let's see, straight out: can you finish your part of the report before Friday?

items.spanish: No es que no quiera ayudarte, es que hoy tengo una reunión detrás de otra.
items.english: It's not that I don't want to help you, it's just that today I have one meeting after another.

items.spanish: Perdón por el inciso, pero creo que empezamos a salirnos del tema.
items.english: Sorry for the aside, but I think we're starting to get off the subject.

items.spanish: Volvamos al tema y vayamos al grano antes de la pausa.
items.english: Let's get back to the topic and get to the point before the break.

sections.content: Even in casual *No es que…, es que…*, the first verb still takes the **subjunctive** because you reject that reason (*No es que no tenga tiempo*, never *No es que no tengo tiempo*), while the second verb after *es que* stays in the **indicative** because it states the real reason.
